courses.sampleLessonTitle: Sample Lesson: Data Cleaning & Revenue Aggregation in Pandas
courses.sampleLessonContent: Before plotting any chart, analysts remove duplicates, standardize string casing, coerce numeric columns, and aggregate cleanly by category.
courses.sampleLessonCode:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("enrollments.csv")
df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["record_id"])
df["course"] = df["course"].str.strip().str.title()
df["completion_rate"] = pd.to_numeric(df["completion_rate"], errors="coerce")
df["completion_rate"] = df["completion_rate"].fillna(df["completion_rate"].median())

summary = (
    df.groupby("course", as_index=False)
      .agg(students=("record_id", "count"), avg_completion=("completion_rate", "mean"))
      .sort_values(by="students", ascending=False)
)
print(summary)

materials.description: Concise study guide covering relational normalization, primary/foreign keys, SELECT filters, GROUP BY, and JOIN types.
materials.previewContent:
# APJ Tech — SQL Notes

1. DDL vs DML: CREATE/ALTER/DROP vs SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.
2. Filtering & Grouping: WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY; HAVING filters aggregated groups.
3. JOIN Summary:
   - INNER JOIN: Matching rows in both tables.
   - LEFT JOIN: All rows from left table + matching right rows.
4. Normalization: Eliminate repeating groups (1NF), partial dependencies (2NF), transitive dependencies (3NF).
